# Pragmatism Derives From the Greek Word for Action

The term,[^1] pragmatism,[^2] is derived from the same Greek word [pi rho alpha gamma mu alpha], meaning action, from which our words 'practice' and 'practical' come.[^3] It was first introduced into philosophy by Mr. Charles Peirce in 1878.[^4]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#History of the Method]] "The term"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#History of the Method]] "pragmatism"
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#History of the Method]] "is derived from the same Greek word [pi rho alpha gamma mu alpha], meaning action, from which our words 'practice' and 'practical' come."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#History of the Method]] "It was first introduced into philosophy by Mr. Charles Peirce in 1878."
